title: Timestamp-safe post-earnings-announcement drift (BTO/AMC classified, sector-neutral SUE long/short)
outcome_blind_attestation: Proposal written before any scored window exists. No candidate returns, PF, Sharpe or rankings were computed, and no other proposal lane's files were read. Literature expectations are qualitative priors only.
priority_space: PLAN_stocks.md section 9: post-earnings drift with timestamp-safe surprise data

economic_mechanism.statement: Quarterly earnings news diffuses slowly into prices because attention-constrained investors underreact to the content of the announcement relative to expectations; prices then drift in the direction of the standardized unexpected earnings (SUE) for roughly one to three months after the release. The family is long high-SUE and short low-SUE names inside each sector, harvesting the drift.
economic_mechanism.counterparty: Attention-constrained investors (discretionary retail and institutions anchored to stale expectations) who trade the news late; plus arbitrageurs who limit participation because the announcement risk premium must be held for weeks. We take the opposite side during the diffusion window.
economic_mechanism.why_the_edge_exists: Limited attention and investor conservatism produce underreaction to earnings content, not to the event calendar itself; the drift persists because the relevant cohorts (individual investors, per Bartov-Radhakrishnan-Krinsky 2000) are slow to incorporate news.

literature.citation: Ball, R. and P. Brown (1968), 'An Empirical Evaluation of Accounting Income Numbers', Journal of Accounting Research 6(2).
literature.claim_used: Origin of the post-earnings drift observation on US equities.

literature.citation: Bernard, V. and J. Thomas (1989), 'Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?', Journal of Accounting Research 27 (Supplement).
literature.claim_used: Drift persists roughly 60 trading days after announcement; SUE-sorted portfolios earn increasing returns in SUE quintiles.

literature.citation: Bernard, V. and J. Thomas (1990), 'Evidence That Stock Prices Do Not Fully Reflect the Implications of Current Earnings for Future Earnings', Journal of Accounting Research 28(2).
literature.claim_used: Underreaction to the implications of current earnings for future earnings; mechanism-level evidence.

literature.citation: Livnat, J. and R. Mendenhall (2006), 'Comparing the Post-Earnings Announcement Drift for Surprises Calculated from Analyst and Time Series Forecasts', Journal of Accounting Research 44(1).
literature.claim_used: Drift exists for both analyst-consensus-based and time-series-based SUE; revenue surprises also drift. Grounds the neighbour arm.

literature.citation: Bartov, E., S. Radhakrishnan and I. Krinsky (2000), 'Investor Sophistication and Patterns in Stock Returns after Earnings Announcements', The Accounting Review 75(1).
literature.claim_used: Drift concentrated where individual investors dominate; identifies the counterparty.

literature.citation: Hong, H. and J. Stein (1999), 'A Unified Theory of Underreaction, Momentum Trading, and Overreaction in Asset Markets', Journal of Finance 54(6); Barberis, N., A. Shleifer and R. Vishny (1998), 'A Model of Investor Sentiment', Journal of Financial Economics 49(3).
literature.claim_used: Theoretical underreaction mechanisms (gradual information diffusion; conservatism).

universe_neutralization_benchmark.universe: PIT-accepted liquid common stocks/ETFs from A3 at each formation date (PLAN section 7 A3 floors: >= 30 eligible names per decision, >= 8y history; delisted names retained through final valid event).
universe_neutralization_benchmark.neutralization: Sector-neutral: within each PIT GICS sector, long top SUE quintile, short bottom SUE quintile, dollar-neutral legs; sector weights capped equal so no sector bet dominates.
universe_neutralization_benchmark.benchmark: Flat (cash) plus SPY total return as declared external benchmark; the declared factor-neutral context is sector-neutral long/short (documented here as the comparison set for scoring later).

clocks.formation_clock: Event-anchored: at each earnings release with a classified timing, compute SUE from PIT snapshots; cohort eligibility is decided at the first regular-session open strictly after the release instant. BTO releases enter that same date's session (news is public before the 09:30 ET open, session_bounds from the calendar). AMC releases enter next_session(date) open. UNKNOWN-timing releases are excluded with a reason (fail closed).
clocks.holding_clock: 60 regular sessions from formation (Bernard-Thomas horizon), implemented as 12 weekly cohorts so the aggregate book is rebalanced weekly by replacing the expired cohort; every session boundary taken from session_bounds/next_session, early closes (13:00 ET) are valid entry/exit session ends and never silently extended to 16:00.
clocks.execution_clock: Entries/exits at the regular-session opening auction of the formation/exit session (first executable point of the session). If a name is halted at the formation open (declared HaltInterval), the name skips to the first session whose opening auction is not covered by a declared halt; unexplained gaps fail closed via classify_gap and no synthetic fill is ever authorized.
clocks.calendar_expressibility: All clocks reduce to session_bounds(day), next_session(after), phase-disabled baseline (pre/post disabled per assert_baseline_scoring_phases) and early_close_cutoff_utc. No weekly or synthetic calendar is used; the calendar manifest digest is part of the trial identity.

turnover_capacity.expected_turnover: Literature-informed prior, not a computed result: with roughly a quarter of the liquid universe announcing per quarter with classified surprises and 60-session holds in weekly cohorts, expected one-sided book turnover is of order 6-10x per year.
turnover_capacity.expected_capacity: Mid eight figures USD notional at <= 5% ADV participation in the quintile tails, dominated by small-cap tail ADV; announcement-cohort clustering concentrates execution on post-announcement days where liquidity is typically above average.
turnover_capacity.cost_sensitivity_declared: Auction/limit cross per side plus borrow on the short leg must clear the S6 stress (x1.5 commission and spread) for any survivor; drift is a known thin-margin family after costs.

arms.name: anchor_eps_sue_ls
arms.definition: Sector-neutral long top-quintile / short bottom-quintile EPS SUE (PIT consensus; frozen fallback = seasonal-random-walk SUE) formed at the timestamp-safe next open, held 60 sessions in weekly cohorts.
arms.role: The drift mechanism as documented in the literature.

arms.name: neighbour_revenue_sue_ls
arms.definition: Identical pipeline, universe, clocks and neutralization, but the surprise is the revenue SUE (actual vs PIT consensus revenue).
arms.role: Theoretically justified neighbour: revenue surprises carry the same underreaction content (Livnat-Mendenhall 2006) because they are the volume counterpart of the same earnings information set; supports the anchor if the mechanism (news-content diffusion), not the EPS accounting construct, is what drifts.

arms.name: control_sign_flipped_sue_ls
arms.definition: Identical pipeline, cohorts, clocks, holdings and costs, but the SUE sign is flipped (long bottom quintile, short top quintile).
arms.role: Causal negative control: it keeps the entire event calendar, portfolio construction and cost structure and removes only the news-content direction. Underreaction predicts the drift disappears or inverts; if the anchor's edge survives sign-flipping, the edge is not news content and the family is falsified.

corporate_action_earnings_borrow_dividen.corporate_actions: All splits/cash dividends applied exactly once at ex/effective timestamps by the A4 CorporateActionEngine; signals computed on the declared TOTAL_RETURN research path, fills on the RAW path; raw-vs-total-return reconciliation records required at every action boundary touched by a holding (SD2/SD5-style goldens).
corporate_action_earnings_borrow_dividen.earnings_during_holding: A new release for a held name replaces its SUE at the next cohort boundary (no intra-cohort churn); the name's own announcement-day trading is never used for formation fills (formation open is strictly after the classified release instant).
corporate_action_earnings_borrow_dividen.borrow: Short legs require PIT locate availability and borrow rate at formation (A5 contract); unavailable borrow rejects the short leg, never fills it for free (PLAN section 7 A5). Short dividend liability accrues to shorts on ex-dates.
corporate_action_earnings_borrow_dividen.dividends: Long legs receive cash dividends (cash_to_position at ex/effective moment); dividend yield recorded per ReconciliationRecord; benchmark comparison uses SPY total return so dividend treatment is symmetric.

falsification_rule.pre_registered: Family survives only if (a) anchor: after-cost expectancy > 0, position PF >= 1.10, >= 2/3 chronological folds positive, no fold PF < 0.80 (PLAN section 13 gates); (b) SUE-quintile monotonicity declared as a diagnostic, not a gate; (c) neighbour supports anchor (same sign, economically similar magnitude); (d) sign-flipped control destroys or materially weakens the anchor effect; (e) drop-one-symbol/sector/fold survival. Failure of (d) while (a) passes means the edge is calendar/event exposure rather than news content and the family is rejected as mechanism-mistitled.
external_validity_caveats: Drift is documented mostly on 1970-2005 US data and is known to weaken post-publication (McLean and Pontiff 2016, Journal of Finance 71(1); retrieval MODEL_INTERNAL_UNVERIFIED); a null result is a legitimate outcome.
Consensus-data PIT quality is the single largest data risk: misaligned estimate snapshots can manufacture or destroy the surprise; any snapshot drift is a new trial identity.
Costs and borrow consume a large fraction of gross drift, especially in the low-liquidity quintile tail.
Cohort clustering makes returns lumpy around macro announcement seasons (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct).
Results depend on the frozen calendar table; 2027-2030 rule-derived entries require provider verification before any sealed-window scoring reaches them.

novelty_defense.vs_rejected_crypto_families: Not a rescue of M01 aggressor-flow absorption (observable is accounting surprise vs expectations, not order-flow imbalance), not funding-carry (no funding cashflows, no perpetual contract), not weekly reversal (no reversal signal, no weekly-calendar clock; the weekly cadence here is only a cohort aggregation of event-anchored 60-session holds). Observable, counterparty, clock and causal control are all different from each listed family.
novelty_defense.vs_other_S2_lanes: Depends on earnings-timestamp PIT classification, which is the A4 lane's owned capability (classify_earnings_timestamp); a lane without that machinery cannot express the formation clock without silently mis-timing AMC names.
